1.2 Introduce an inducible CRISPRa module (dCas9-VPR or dCas9-p300core) with multiple gRNAs tiled across the CDX2 promoter/enhancers. Build a microfluidic-compatible induction system (doxycycline or small-molecule–gated) enabling pulse widths from 15 min to 24 h.
1.3 Establish baseline differentiation using a chemically defined renal induction protocol (e.g., Activin A/BMP4/RA followed by GDNF/FGF/Wnt modulation) and quantify day-by-day emergence of CITED1+ and SIX2+ populations.

Step 2: Detailed implementation of the adapted methodology.
2.1 Methodological adaptation: Replace constant morphogen-only differentiation with a closed-loop, pulse-width–modulated Cdx2 induction layered on top of the same morphogen schedule. Use real-time CITED1 reporter readout as feedback to tune Cdx2 pulse width/amplitude (control algorithm: Bayesian optimization or PID-like rule) toward maximizing the area-under-curve of CITED1+ fraction while constraining off-target lineage markers.
2.2 Execute a Cdx2 pulse-scan matrix: vary pulse width (0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 h) and timing window (day 0–1, 1–2, 2–3) while holding morphogens constant. Include a sustained-Cdx2 condition as a negative control for lineage drift.
2.3 Quantify mechanism: perform time-resolved multi-omics on sorted populations (CITED1+/−; SIX2+/−): (i) scRNA-seq for lineage trajectories and cell-state entropy; (ii) scATAC-seq to measure enhancer priming at IM/nephrogenic loci; (iii) CUT&Tag for CDX2 occupancy and H3K27ac changes at renal competence regions. Test whether transient CDX2 occupancy precedes accessibility gains at IM-associated enhancers and whether sustained CDX2 maintains accessibility at extra-renal programs.
2.4 Differentiate optimized CITED1+ progenitors into proximal tubule, podocyte-precursor, and collecting duct lineages using established cues; compare maturation markers and functional assays (albumin uptake for proximal tubule; nephrin/podocin for podocyte lineage; AQP2/ENaC components for collecting duct).
2.5 Drug screening build: plate standardized renal derivatives (or mini-organoids) into 384-well format; implement multiplex readouts: viability, mitochondrial stress, KIM-1/HAVCR1 induction, γH2AX DNA damage, and transporter function (e.g., OCT2/MATE activity assays). Screen a reference nephrotoxin panel (cisplatin, gentamicin, amphotericin B, tenofovir, ifosfamide metabolites) plus matched non-nephrotoxic controls.

Step 3: Rigorous validation and analytical framework.
3.1 Benchmark heterogeneity and reproducibility: compare coefficient of variation across batches/lines for CITED1+ yield, renal lineage composition, and drug-response EC50/LOEC values between (A) morphogens-only and (B) Cdx2-pulse + morphogens.
3.2 Causality tests: (i) CDX2 loss-of-function (CRISPRi or siRNA) to show necessity of the pulse; (ii) substitute CDX2 activation with a non-posterior TF (control) to test specificity; (iii) block Wnt/FGF signaling during the pulse to test pathway dependency of the priming mechanism.
3.3 Predictive performance: compute sensitivity/specificity for known nephrotoxins, and evaluate assay concordance with clinical/animal data. Use dose-response modeling and hierarchical Bayesian batch correction to quantify improvement attributable to the adaptation.
3.4 Safety/lineage fidelity: assess off-target differentiation (trophectoderm/intestinal markers), karyotype stability, and long-term epigenetic drift across passages.
Feasibility:
1. Theoretical/Empirical Basis: hPSC-to-renal differentiation under defined morphogens can yield CITED1+ progenitor populations and renal cell types suitable for drug testing; PSC gene regulatory networks exhibit state transitions that are highly sensitive to timed transcription factor perturbations, and Cdx2 is a known driver of distinct fate attractors whose effects depend on signal context and duration.
2. Transfer Logic (How the adaptation fits the domain): The adaptation imports a control-systems principle (pulse-width modulation with feedback) into developmental bioengineering by converting a static TF perturbation into a precisely timed, quantitatively tunable input that reshapes chromatin and lineage competence. Using CRISPRa avoids permanent genome rewiring and enables reversible, titratable activation compatible with manufacturing and screening workflows.
3. Comparative Advantage: Compared to morphogen-only protocols, the Cdx2-pulse circuit is designed to (i) reduce stochastic entry into competing lineages by synchronizing early competence, (ii) expand and stabilize the CITED1+ progenitor reservoir (higher yield, lower variance), and (iii) improve downstream drug-screen signal-to-noise and cross-batch reproducibility, directly addressing a core limitation of PSC-derived renal models for high-throughput nephrotoxicity screening.
Critique: This is a technically ambitious and unusually well-specified proposal that integrates developmental biology, epigenomic mechanism, and control-systems engineering. Engineering resolution is very high: reporter knock-ins, CRISPRa pulse control, multi-omics, and microfluidic-compatible induction are all actionable with current technology, though the closed-loop real-time optimization using reporter feedback is nontrivial and may face latency/noise constraints that are not fully addressed. Logical consistency is strong: the hypothesis that transient Cdx2 pulses can bias posterior mesoderm competence without trophectoderm commitment is mechanistically plausible and supported by chromatin priming logic, but it rests on a narrow temporal window that may vary across hPSC lines more than acknowledged. Evidence grounding is solid and stays within renal developmental and stem cell biology; however, direct prior evidence for Cdx2-mediated IM priming (as opposed to axial/posterior bias) is inferential rather than established. Rationale quality is high, as the proposal directly targets a known bottleneck—batch heterogeneity and poor predictive power in PSC-derived renal drug screens—via a genuinely creative control-theoretic intervention rather than incremental optimization.

Hypothesis:
PSC-RANTES produces unusually durable CCR5 down-modulation because it shifts post-endocytic fate at a defined sorting checkpoint: after canonical β-arrestin/AP-2/clathrin internalization, PSC-RANTES–phosphorylated CCR5 preferentially engages an endosome-to-TGN retrieval axis composed of the retromer core (VPS35–VPS26–VPS29) plus a restricted set of SNX adaptors (primary candidates: SNX27; secondary candidates: SNX1/2 with SNX5/6; and WASH/FAM21 as the actin-polymerization effector). This retrieval engagement diverts CCR5 away from Rab4/Rab11-mediated recycling and/or degradative routing, producing TGN sequestration that is functionally equivalent to long-lived desensitization (reduced surface receptor, impaired resensitization).

Mechanistic rationale addressing reviewer gaps: (i) retromer does not typically bind GPCRs directly—cargo selection is frequently mediated by SNX adaptors and sequence motifs (e.g., PDZ-binding for SNX27 cargos) and can be strongly modulated by receptor phosphorylation “barcodes” that control adaptor handoff; thus we pre-specify SNX nodes and explicitly test whether CCR5 uses an SNX27-like PDZ module or an SNX-BAR/WASH-dependent pathway. (ii) TGN sequestration will be distinguished from generic endosomal retention by orthogonal evidence: time-resolved colocalization with TGN markers and retrieval intermediates, functional dependence on VPS35/SNX/WASH, and demonstration of increased endosome→TGN flux (not merely slowed recycling). (iii) The engineered ‘sorting switch’ will be designed to be phosphorylation-gated without constitutive binding by separating (a) a GRK2/3-tuned phospho-acceptor cassette that is only modified under agonist-activated CCR5, from (b) a docking module whose affinity is masked until phosphorylation triggers a local conformational/charge change; additionally, a failsafe inducible-recruitment variant will be included to enforce conditionality if phospho-gating is leaky.

For the CXCR4 arm, we do not assume generic clathrin/AP-2 scarcity. Instead, we test a quantitative ‘shared-node competition’ model at the specific retrieval/sorting layer (retromer/SNX/WASH) and in parallel test alternative cross-desensitization mechanisms (GRK/β-arrestin redistribution, kinase sequestration, endosomal signaling cross-talk). We predict that heterologous CXCR4 desensitization—if present—will scale with measurable occupancy/saturation of shared sorting effectors (β-arrestin-2 and/or retromer/WASH) rather than bulk clathrin/AP-2, and that selective replenishment of the limiting node will rescue CXCR4 responsiveness.
Plan:
Step 0 — Engineering acceptance gates (prevents misinterpretation of ‘handoff’):
0.1 Construct strategy: endogenous-locus CCR5 and CXCR4 CRISPR knock-in in Jurkat-derived CD4+ T cell–like cells (and HEK293 as imaging-optimized control) using minimal tags: (i) an extracellular 1× HA or ALFA epitope in the N-terminus for pulse-chase surface labeling (inserted after signal peptide to preserve trafficking), (ii) a small intracellular tag for proximity labeling (TurboID-mini or APEX2) fused to the C-terminus via a flexible (GGGGS)2 linker, and (iii) optional HaloTag on a subset of constructs only in HEK293 for single-particle tracking. All edits will be heterozygous first, then homozygous only if acceptance gates pass.
0.2 Acceptance gates for every CCR5 ‘switch’ variant (must pass all before trafficking interpretation):
  - Surface expression: flow cytometry with anti-HA/ALFA at 4°C; acceptance ≥70% of WT median fluorescence (endogenous WT knock-in control).
  - Ligand binding: fluorescent CCL5 and PSC-RANTES binding (or radioligand if available); acceptance: KD within 3× of WT and saturable binding.
  - G-protein coupling: acute Gi signaling (cAMP suppression assay) and Ca2+ flux; acceptance: Emax ≥70% of WT for CCL5 and PSC-RANTES; potency shift ≤5×.
  - β-arrestin recruitment: NanoBiT or BRET (CCR5–SmBiT / β-arrestin2–LgBiT or equivalent); acceptance: PSC-RANTES produces robust recruitment comparable to WT (≥70% AUC), and CCL5 recruitment is not artificially abolished.
  - Basal activity/leakiness: basal internalization and basal β-arrestin signal must be ≤1.5× WT.

Step 1 — Mechanistically discriminative trafficking map with explicit TGN-retrieval nodes:
1.1 Compartment markers (imaging + biochemical fractionation):
  - Internalization: clathrin light chain (CLTA) and AP2M1; early endosome: EEA1/Rab5; recycling: Rab4/Rab11; late endosome/lysosome: Rab7/LAMP1; TGN: TGN46 and Golgin-97; endosome-to-TGN retrieval intermediates: SNX6 (SNX-BAR), SNX27, VPS35, FAM21 (WASH complex).
1.2 Stimulation design: PSC-RANTES vs CCL5 matched by receptor occupancy (dose normalized to equal initial β-arrestin recruitment AUC to separate trafficking effects from different activation magnitudes). Time course: 0, 2, 5, 10, 20, 40, 90, 180 min; washout + recovery: 1, 2, 4, 8, 24 h.
1.3 Quantification: automated segmentation with per-receptor ‘fate fractions’ (surface, EE, recycling endosome, TGN, lysosome). Include a kinetic compartmental model with explicit endosome→TGN flux term (k_ETGN) distinct from recycling (k_ER) and degradation (k_ED). Model selection will compare: (A) increased k_ETGN, (B) decreased k_ER, (C) increased k_internalization only.
1.4 Orthogonal validation that signal is true TGN retrieval (not generic retention):
  - Brefeldin A (Golgi/TGN disruption) and temperature block (20°C) assays to perturb TGN trafficking; predict loss of PSC-RANTES-induced ‘TGN accumulation’ if it is genuine retrieval.
  - Endosome-to-TGN cargo control (e.g., CI-MPR) co-trafficking behavior to benchmark retrieval pathway integrity.

Step 2 — Pre-specified candidate TGN-sorting nodes and epistasis logic (mandatory directive #1):
2.1 Candidate node list (tested in a defined order):
  - Retromer core: VPS35, VPS26A/B, VPS29.
  - SNX adaptors:
    (Primary) SNX27 (PDZ-domain cargo adaptor often linked to recycling and retromer coupling; tested for CCR5 engagement via engineered PDZ-binding options and endogenous association).
    (Secondary) SNX1/2 with SNX5/6 (SNX-BAR tubulation module associated with retromer-mediated retrieval) and the WASH complex (FAM21) as effector.
  - Controls/alternates: GGA adaptors and AP-1 (TGN sorting), to ensure the phenotype is retrieval-specific rather than generic TGN retention.
2.2 Perturbation architecture:
  - Acute depletion: AID2 (auxin-inducible degron) or dTAG on VPS35 and SNX27 (fast, reversible) in HEK293; inducible CRISPRi (dCas9-KRAB) in Jurkat-like cells for longer assays.
  - Epistasis design: For each perturbation, measure (i) CCR5 internalization rate (k_int), (ii) k_ETGN (from model), (iii) TGN colocalization fraction at 40–180 min, (iv) surface recovery half-life post-washout.
  - Decision criteria:
    *If PSC-RANTES phenotype requires VPS35 and SNX6/WASH (but not SNX27):* supports SNX-BAR/WASH tubulation retrieval route.
    *If requires SNX27 and VPS35:* supports SNX27-retromer cargo adaptor mechanism.
    *If independent of retromer/SNX but sensitive to AP-1/GGA:* suggests alternative TGN sorting not retromer retrieval.
2.3 Interaction validation (co-IP + proximity labeling with time-window control):
  - Proximity labeling: CCR5-miniTurboID or CCR5-APEX2 biotinylation in short windows (e.g., 0–5, 5–15, 15–40, 40–90 min) after PSC-RANTES vs CCL5; streptavidin pulldown + targeted PRM mass spectrometry for VPS35, VPS26, SNX27, SNX6, FAM21, AP-1.
  - Co-IP: crosslinker-assisted co-IP (DSP) at matched timepoints to validate direct/complex association.
  - Quantitative readout: enrichment fold-change normalized to receptor abundance and internalization extent.

Step 3 — Engineering the phospho-gated ‘sorting switch’ with explicit chemical/architectural parameters (mandatory directive #3):
3.1 Switch designs (two-tier, with a failsafe):
  - Design A (phospho-exposed PDZ ligand): Insert a short C-terminal helix + PDZ-binding motif (Class I: -[S/T]-X-Φ, e.g., -STVL) preceded by a GRK2/3-favored phosphocluster (6–8 Ser/Thr within ~15 aa, enriched in acidic context to favor GRK2/3). Rationale: phosphorylation can electrostatically unmask the PDZ ligand by disrupting membrane-proximal basic residues and/or intramolecular packing, enabling SNX27 engagement only after activation.
  - Design B (phospho-primed 14-3-3 gate controlling adaptor recruitment): Embed a high-specificity 14-3-3 binding site (mode I RSXpSXP) adjacent to a masked docking peptide for a retromer/SNX-interacting module. Upon phosphorylation, 14-3-3 binding changes local conformation to expose the docking element. This reduces constitutive adaptor binding risk.
  - Failsafe Design C (inducible recruitment): CCR5 fused to FRB and an endosome/TGN adaptor module fused to FKBP; rapalog addition recruits the adaptor only when desired, providing a non-phospho-dependent contingency to prove causality between recruitment and TGN sequestration.
3.2 Library and build constraints:
  - Small, interpretable library: 6–10 barcode variants varying Ser/Thr spacing and local charge; 2 docking motif variants per design; total ≤20 constructs.
  - Expression control: single-copy landing pad in HEK293 for screening; then best 3 moved to CCR5 locus in Jurkat-like cells.
3.3 Mechanistic verification that the switch rewires sorting (not activation):
  - Re-run acceptance gates (Step 0).
  - Demonstrate preserved β-arrestin recruitment kinetics but altered post-endocytic associations (increased SNX/retromer proximity labeling after PSC-RANTES without increased initial internalization).

Step 4 — CXCR4 heterologous desensitization: quantitative capacity/competition and alternative hypotheses (mandatory directive #2):
4.1 Capacity/competition experiments with explicit saturation logic:
  - Dose-response matrix: PSC-RANTES concentration × exposure time to generate graded CCR5 internalization and graded retromer/SNX/WASH occupancy.
  - Measure limiting-node occupancy directly:
    * β-arrestin2 redistribution: live-cell imaging of β-arrestin2-mScarlet knock-in (or Halo) with CCR5; quantify fraction of β-arrestin in endosomal puncta.
    * Retromer/WASH occupancy: VPS35-GFP or FAM21-GFP knock-in in HEK293; quantify puncta intensity and colocalization with CCR5 endosomes.
  - CXCR4 functional assays: CXCL12-induced Ca2+ flux and receptor internalization after PSC-RANTES pretreatment.
  - Rescue-by-titration: re-express candidate limiting factors (β-arrestin2, VPS35, SNX27, FAM21) under doxycycline-tunable promoter across a defined range; criterion for competition model: CXCR4 responsiveness is restored in proportion to the replenished node and correlates with reduced occupancy.
4.2 Alternative hypotheses and discriminating readouts:
  - GRK sequestration: measure GRK2/3 membrane recruitment and availability (BRET-based GRK translocation sensor); test whether GRK overexpression rescues CXCR4.
  - β-arrestin redistribution (without clathrin limitation): compare effect of β-arrestin2 overexpression vs AP-2 overexpression; competition model predicts β-arrestin rescue > AP-2 rescue.
  - Endosomal signaling cross-talk: assay ERK phosphorylation and endosomal G protein signaling reporters; block with MEK inhibitor or endocytosis inhibitors to see if CXCR4 desensitization depends on downstream signaling rather than trafficking capacity.
  - CXCR4-specific ubiquitination program: quantify CXCR4 ubiquitination (IP-western) and test E3 ligase involvement (e.g., AIP4/ITCH literature pathway) to rule in/out independent regulation.

Step 5 — Causality, translational relevance, and success criteria:
5.1 Causality tests:
  - For top ‘TGN-locking’ switch: show prolonged surface down-modulation and impaired resensitization without changes in k_int; then abolish phenotype by acute VPS35/SNX/WASH depletion (epistasis).
  - For ‘fast-recycling’ switch: show accelerated surface recovery and preserved signaling.
5.2 Primary cell validation:
  - Introduce 1–2 best designs into primary CD4+ T cells and macrophages via CRISPR knock-in (RNP + AAV6 donor) with minimal tags.
  - Outcomes: duration of R5-tropic HIV-1 entry inhibition after PSC-RANTES washout; chemotaxis impairment duration (CCR5 ligands); reversibility (recovery of CCR5 surface and signaling).
5.3 Explicit success criteria (go/no-go):
  - Mechanism: PSC-RANTES increases k_ETGN (model) by ≥2× vs CCL5 and this increase is VPS35- and at least one SNX/WASH-dependent.
  - Engineering: at least one switch variant produces a programmable ≥3× change in CCR5 surface recovery half-life (vs WT) while passing acceptance gates.
  - CXCR4: if heterologous desensitization observed, it must (a) correlate with quantified occupancy of a specific limiting node and (b) be rescued by titrated replenishment of that node; otherwise, pivot to the best-supported alternative mechanism from 4.2.

Risk mitigation:
  - Tag/misfolding risk: minimal epitopes; heterozygous validation; immediate elimination if acceptance gates fail.
  - Phospho-conditional leakage: advance only variants with low basal internalization/association; deploy failsafe Design C to prove causality even if phospho-gating is imperfect.
  - Ambiguity of ‘TGN sequestration’: require triple evidence—TGN colocalization, retrieval-intermediate dependence (VPS35/SNX/WASH), and sensitivity to TGN trafficking perturbations.
Feasibility:
1) Why the mechanism is now sufficiently specified: The proposal pre-defines the exact retrieval machinery to test (VPS35/VPS26/VPS29; SNX27; SNX1/2–SNX5/6; WASH/FAM21) and lays out an epistasis framework that distinguishes true endosome→TGN retrieval from generic endosomal retention or slowed recycling. Time-window proximity labeling plus targeted MS and crosslinker co-IP provide orthogonal interaction evidence, while acute degrons/CRISPRi provide causal dependence.

2) Why phospho-gated engineering is interpretable and de-risked: Each switch variant is gated by explicit acceptance criteria (surface expression, ligand binding, Gi signaling, β-arrestin recruitment, low basal activity), ensuring that altered trafficking is not conflated with altered receptor activation or folding. The switch architectures include mechanistic safeguards against constitutive binding (phospho-unmasking or 14-3-3 gating) and a reversible inducible-dimerization failsafe that can enforce conditional recruitment to directly test sufficiency.

3) Why the CXCR4 arm is no longer a logical leap: Instead of assuming clathrin/AP-2 limitation, the plan quantitatively tests whether a specific shared node is limiting (β-arrestin2 and/or retromer/SNX/WASH) using occupancy metrics, saturation dose–response designs, and rescue-by-titration. In parallel, it enumerates and experimentally discriminates alternative explanations (GRK sequestration, β-arrestin redistribution, endosomal signaling cross-talk, CXCR4 ubiquitination control), preventing post hoc interpretation.

4) Practical feasibility: All methods are standard in modern receptor trafficking studies (CRISPR knock-in tagging, automated imaging with compartment markers, AID/dTAG depletion, TurboID/APEX2 proximity labeling, kinetic modeling). The design reduces scope risk by (i) screening constructs in a controlled landing-pad system, (ii) limiting library size, and (iii) defining explicit go/no-go criteria that prevent resource-intensive primary cell work until mechanism and engineering performance are demonstrated.
Critique: The work is unusually well-specified for GPCR trafficking and earns high marks for pre-defined nodes, orthogonal assays, and go/no-go gates. Primary weaknesses are: (i) the central mechanistic leap—PSC-RANTES encoding a phosphorylation barcode that biases CCR5 into endosome→TGN retrieval—is plausible but still under-justified at the sequence/structural level (i.e., what CCR5 C-tail motifs or known SNX27-PDZ compatibility exist, and which GRKs are expected to write the barcode in the relevant T-cell context). (ii) The engineered switch designs risk conflating engineered adaptor engagement with non-physiologic trafficking (particularly SNX27, which often supports recycling rather than TGN retrieval in many contexts), so interpretation will hinge on demonstrating genuine retrieval intermediates and directionality beyond colocalization. (iii) The CXCR4 arm is improved by the shared-node saturation framework, but it remains biologically uncertain whether retromer/WASH capacity is limiting at physiologic expression levels in Jurkat-like cells; without careful stoichiometric calibration and expression control, rescue-by-overexpression can create artifacts that mimic ‘competition’.

Hypothesis: Lineage-accelerated nonsynonymous substitutions in E(z) re-tune PRC2 catalytic output (H3K27me3 product profile and residence time) by altering an allosteric coupling pathway between the SET catalytic core and partner-binding regions, which in turn changes the threshold for PRC1 (Psc-containing) recruitment at PREs organized by Zeste/Ph, ultimately shifting homeotic gene repression stability. Methodological adaptation: we will engineer a DNA-barcoded, nucleosome-tethered “PRC recruitment rheostat” (a modular PRE mimic) that converts PRC2 catalysis into a quantitative, multiplex readout of PRC1 capture in vivo—overcoming the limitation that native chromatin context confounds causal attribution of E(z) amino-acid substitutions to PRC1 recruitment and homeotic silencing.
Plan:
Step 1: Build a multiplexed PRE–nucleosome recruitment rheostat panel.
- Design a library of synthetic PRE cassettes containing: (i) Zeste motifs, (ii) Pho/Pho-like motifs (as the PcG DNA-anchoring control), and (iii) tunable spacing/valency to emulate PRE architecture; each cassette is paired with a unique 18–20 bp DNA barcode.
- Embed each cassette upstream of a minimal promoter driving a short-lived reporter (e.g., destabilized GFP) plus MS2 stem loops for nascent transcription imaging.
- Genomically integrate the cassette library as a single-copy landing-pad array at a neutral locus in Drosophila (or Drosophila-derived cell lines), ensuring identical chromosomal position effects across variants.

Step 2: Methodological adaptation—nucleosome-tethered PRC “capture” with catalytic-state sensing.
- Adapt split-enzyme proximity labeling into a chromatin-state–dependent capture system: fuse TurboID-half A to Psc (PRC1) and TurboID-half B to a chromatin reader that binds H3K27me3 (engineered CBX/HP1-like chromodomain with calibrated affinity). Reconstitution occurs only when PRC1 is within nanometers of H3K27me3-marked nucleosomes at the rheostat cassette.
- Engineer an E(z) variant panel derived from evolutionary rate hotspots (dN/dS-informed) but implemented as domain-swapped micro-alleles (short motif replacements rather than full-length allele swaps) to isolate mechanistic coupling: (i) ancestral-motif, (ii) derived-motif, (iii) catalytic-dead control, (iv) allosteric-pathway disruption mutants predicted from coevolutionary coupling analysis of PRC2 subunits.
- Readout: biotinylation is captured by streptavidin pulldown followed by barcode sequencing (BioID-Barcode-seq). This yields a quantitative “PRC1 capture index” per PRE cassette per E(z) variant.
- In parallel, quantify catalytic output by CUT&Tag at the barcoded array using spike-in normalization for H3K27me1/2/3, enabling product-profile shifts to be linked to PRC1 capture.
- Introduce controlled nuclear pH perturbations only as a stress test (not as the primary method): use genetically encoded pH clamps (v-ATPase modulators) to probe whether E(z) substitutions buffer PRC recruitment under physiological challenge.

Step 3: Rigorous validation, mechanism tests, and homeotic gene linkage.
- Mechanistic causality: (i) correlate PRC1 capture index with H3K27me3/2 ratios across PRE architectures; (ii) fit a kinetic threshold model where PRC1 capture depends on local H3K27me3 density and predicted E(z) residence time.
- Validate physical interfaces without imaging polytenes: perform crosslinking mass spectrometry (XL-MS) on PRC2 purified from each E(z) background to detect allosteric/interaction rearrangements; compare to functional PRC1 capture shifts.
- Functional consequence: using the same E(z) variants, measure derepression sensitivity of endogenous homeotic genes (Ubx, Abd-B) by precision nuclear run-on sequencing (PRO-seq) and H3K27me3 CUT&Tag at their PREs; test whether variants that lower PRC1 capture at rheostats also destabilize homeotic silencing.
- Controls: Pho/Phol depletion to confirm dependency on canonical PRE anchoring; Zeste motif ablation in rheostats to isolate Zeste-mediated organization; Psc catalytic/interaction mutants to confirm capture specificity.
- Statistical framework: hierarchical Bayesian model to partition variance attributable to (a) PRE architecture, (b) E(z) motif state, (c) interaction term (epistasis), with multiple-testing control over barcodes.
Feasibility:
1. Theoretical/Empirical Basis: PcG repression is mediated by PRC2-catalyzed H3K27 methylation and PRC1 (including Psc) recruitment; Drosophila studies show PcG proteins remain chromatin-associated while specific DNA-binding components (e.g., Pho/Phol) are critical for robust homeotic repression, and evolutionary analyses indicate accelerated nonsynonymous substitution in E(z) with signatures of positive selection. These support a model where E(z) substitutions can alter catalytic output and thereby PRC1 recruitment thresholds.
2. Transfer Logic (How the adaptation fits the domain): The proposal bioengineers an epigenetic “sensor-actuator” assay that converts chromatin enzymology into a multiplexable quantitative readout, enabling mechanistic dissection of adaptive amino-acid changes in an epigenetic regulator—directly relevant to biomedical epigenetics where PRC2/PRC1 dysregulation drives developmental disorders and cancers.
3. Comparative Advantage: Unlike static chromatin staining or locus-by-locus assays, the recruitment rheostat provides (i) controlled PRE architecture, (ii) single-copy genomic context, and (iii) high-throughput, quantitative coupling of PRC2 catalytic state to PRC1 proximity via split proximity labeling and barcode sequencing. This structurally novel platform isolates causality between E(z) substitutions, H3K27 methylation product profiles, PRC1 (Psc) capture, and downstream homeotic gene repression—without relying on live polytene imaging or generic tagging workflows.
Critique: This is an unusually sophisticated and ambitious proposal with strong mechanistic intent. The engineered PRE–nucleosome rheostat and barcode-coupled PRC1 capture readout represent a genuine advance over locus-by-locus PcG assays, and the attempt to isolate allosteric effects of lineage-accelerated E(z) substitutions via micro-allelic swaps is conceptually rigorous. However, several deductions are warranted. First, the split-TurboID reconstitution strategy relies on a narrow spatial and kinetic window that may conflate residence time with labeling efficiency; without explicit calibration of chromodomain affinity and biotinylation kinetics, quantitative interpretation of the 'PRC1 capture index' could be nonlinear or saturating. Second, while synthetic PRE architecture is thoughtfully parameterized, the assumption that Zeste/Pho-driven organization at an ectopic neutral locus faithfully recapitulates endogenous PRE cooperativity remains only partially justified. Third, the evolutionary logic would be strengthened by clearer justification that short motif swaps preserve PRC2 assembly and global stability, rather than introducing cryptic folding or stoichiometric defects. These issues do not undermine feasibility but introduce interpretive risk that slightly weakens logical closure between E(z) substitution, catalytic retuning, and PRC1 threshold behavior.
